neighbours.label: the Black civil-rights struggle in the United States: its figures, places and events (Malcolm X, Dr. King, Freedom Riders, segregation); not women's suffrage or other history
fire: Rosa Parks was arrested in Montgomery in 1955 for refusing to give up her seat on a segregated bus.
Medgar Evers organised voter registration drives for the NAACP in Mississippi.
Four students began a sit-in at a whites-only lunch counter in Greensboro in 1960.
Marchers led by John Lewis were beaten on the bridge in Selma in 1965.
Malcolm X spoke in Harlem about black pride and self-defence.
Dr. King wrote his famous letter from a jail cell in Birmingham.
The Supreme Court ruled in 1954 that racial segregation in public schools was unconstitutional.
The Freedom Riders were attacked by a mob at the bus station in Alabama.
quiet: Amelia Earhart took off from Miami in 1937 on her attempt to fly around the world.
Susan B. Anthony organised petition drives for women's suffrage in New York.
Four students began a chess club at a small public library in Greensboro in 1960.
Runners led by a local champion crossed the bridge in Boston in 1965.
Mark Twain spoke in Hartford about riverboats and his travels abroad.
Dr. Salk tested his famous vaccine in a laboratory in Pittsburgh.
The Supreme Court ruled in 1954 that the tax on imported steel was lawful.
The Wright brothers were greeted by a crowd at the train station in Ohio.

notes: The other side of the same distinction: the + pole fires in women's-suffrage and women's-rights text and promotes ' suff' / ' equality'. This pole's top examples also include gay and transgender rights and one unrelated maths syllabus line; those are not tested here.
